speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping where you wake up frightened. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me if these episodes happen in your bed or if you run out of your room completely?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terror Disorder).

The history of sudden awakening with intense fear, crying, no subsequent confusion, and preserved memory (can be consoled) strongly points to Night Terrors rather than nightmares, which typically involve lucid recall and fear of a specific dream content. I will not request further tests as the clinical presentation is classic; however, if you wish, I can review a sleep study if symptoms persist or worsen.
